paragraphs: Modern military aircraft and aerospace avionics platforms incorporate streaming autonomous agents to assist pilots with flight trajectory optimization, radar threat classification, and emergency subsystem diagnostics. Software operating in airborne flight management systems must never crash or suffer memory leaks: even a microscopic leak of a few bytes per second can cause flight computer memory exhaustion during long-duration maritime patrol or refueling missions.

Our sovereign aerospace avionics streaming architecture is implemented in strict MISRA-C and Rust embedded environments with zero dynamic heap allocation during flight operations. All memory buffers—including ring buffers, circular attention queues, and sensor telemetry structures—are statically allocated at cold system boot and verified via formal mathematical proofs.

The streaming telemetry monitor enforces bounded execution time limits and cycle-accurate memory accounting. If a streaming inference token takes longer than 15ms or an internal stack pointer drifts beyond pre-calculated static boundaries, the hardware watchdog triggers an instantaneous deterministic state reset without disrupting flight control surfaces.

Certified ready for RTCA DO-178C Level A and DO-254 flight hardware certification, the architecture has undergone over 10,000 continuous hours of simulated high-altitude flight operations with absolute zero memory leaks, zero heap fragmentation, and 100% deterministic real-time responsiveness.

faqs.question: How can complex AI models run without dynamic memory allocation?
faqs.answer: All tensor memory pages, KV cache blocks, and workspace buffers are pre-dimensioned and statically reserved during system initialization.

faqs.question: Does this software interface with military avionics data buses like MIL-STD-1553 and ARINC 429?
faqs.answer: Yes. The architecture includes certified low-level bus drivers that ingest 1553 and ARINC datagrams directly into static ring buffers.

faqs.question: What happens if a sensor line suffers catastrophic electrical interference during flight?
faqs.answer: Input validation guards filter corrupted frames before they reach the inference pipeline, logging the bus fault to the flight data recorder.
